decision: Hook configuration is merged per agent across their dedicated config files, with idempotent updates based on script filename matching rather than full command strings. The system supports five agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot), each with agent-specific configuration locations, and unconditionally installs hooks for selected agents.
why: Merging preserves existing project configuration that copying would destroy. Script filename matching survives version bumps where full command comparison would leave stale entries beside new ones. The sessionStart hook injection point was chosen because beforeSubmitPrompt hooks cannot inject context. Unconditional installation keeps the system model-agnostic rather than betting on which agent a contributor uses. Copilot receives a static prompt-type hook rather than a command hook due to its architectural constraints around stdout handling.
evolution: Started with sessionStart as the reliable context-injection point for Cursor, replacing beforeSubmitPrompt which lacked injection capability (ms-5e1a9d44:d1). Established script filename as the stable update key to survive version changes and flag additions (ms-7b3f1e92:d1). Generalized the merge framework to multiple agents by wiring through core.py's existing merge functions, adding Copilot as a fifth agent with different hook constraints (ms-5e366ef4:d2).

decision: Inbox items are promoted conservatively based on evidence of actionability; overlapping proposals are consolidated into a single capability crosswalk that supersedes individual sources, with every workstream assigned exactly one owner to prevent competing contracts. Assessment artifacts are classified as reference material, not inbox items, because the inbox holds untriaged captures while reference holds source material that feeds active work.
why: The inbox accumulated stale, overlapping proposals drafted against outdated assumptions. A distilled crosswalk proved more accurate than the sources, which systematically understated shipped capability. One active owner per workstream prevents duplicate lifecycle tracking, makes dependencies explicit, and renders the roadmap trustworthy. Moving assessment documents to reference removes inbox ambiguity: documents fully evaluated against project lanes belong to reference, while only raw, untriaged captures belong to inbox.
evolution: Established conservative triage criteria, promoting only actionable items with evidence (mse_d2daxtnv8eqx4vqr:d1). Sequenced platform ideas with explicit gates after React Trail parity (mse_mazbt6cek8m8a6st:d1). Unified workstream ownership to prevent competing contracts and explicit dependencies (mse_ddba1ztxqhasfbwf:d2). Rewrote the roadmap document against live code and CHANGELOG, introducing the capability crosswalk as the surviving record and retiring overlapping proposals (mse_wjntbg88n3m0qjss:d1, mse_tx1c338ca1ybr666:d1). Answered Living Archive proposal section 14 selectively, deferring naming and commercialisation questions (mse_y9q4bnv2yckk6w74:d1). Moved triaged assessment artifacts to reference lane, leaving inbox empty (mse_2geqfa8tg182a77p:d1).

decision: integration_mode is a project-local configuration setting read from .memory-seed/project.yaml as a scalar field, determining whether changes integrate via local-merge or PR. The default is local-merge, applied fail-open when the file, field, or value is absent or unrecognised.
why: Fail-open behavior keeps every legacy or unconfigured project unchanged, making the setting purely additive. Surfacing the active mode in ESR preflights makes it visible which integration flow is in effect. The setting is foundation for downstream features like OpenSSF PR-flow requirements and agent contracts that honor the chosen mode.
evolution: Implemented the feature in a single tranche (mse_t388apx6evvmmd1r:d1) with core reader using the same fail-open stdlib line-scanner style as existing project metadata readers, DEFAULT_INTEGRATION_MODE constant, and ESR surfacing in a new Integration mode section.

decision: The link audit writes inert stubs with machine-detected candidate edges, classified but not yet live. Only explicit human approval converts a stub into an actual edge. Negative verdicts—entries whose candidates were all judged unrelated—are recorded rather than left unexamined.
why: A mechanical candidate generator should not author lineage; that remains a deliberate human act. Keeping stubs inert separates the cheap claim "might be related" from the graph claim "IS related." Recording negative verdicts distinguishes "looked and found nothing" from "never looked," both important states for maintenance and completeness.
evolution: Proposed the lifecycle-link authoring assist scaffold with inert stubs containing entry_id and commented candidate evidence that authors would resolve into real edges (mse_jg33a730vpr4085a:d1). Implemented and executed the audit for two dates, creating inert stub files with classified candidates and flagging five cases where the evolves litmus read clearly, withholding approval conversion pending user decision (mse_63qcaab119xmyx0b:d2).
